title: When a new support ticket is created, I want to automatically assign it to the right agent based on
job_to_be_done: When a new support ticket is created, I want to automatically assign it to the right agent based on skill and workload, so I can reduce response times and avoid misassignments.
painful_workflow: Manually reviewing each ticket, reading context, and assigning to the right agent via dropdown in the ticketing system.
current_workaround: Team lead manually reviews each ticket, reads context, assigns to the right agent via dropdown in the ticketing system.
verified_facts: SIG-0004 reports that a team lead manually reviews and assigns each ticket via dropdown (single source).
SIG-0004 reports a consequence of slow response times, misassignments, team-lead bottleneck, and 15-20 min/day of reassignment effort (single source, unverified).
The cluster is supported by exactly 1 independent source and 1 source type.
The workflow recurs per ticket-creation event, i.e., potentially multiple times daily.
inferences: Automatic ticket assignment (round-robin, skill-based, and load-based routing) is a mature, standard feature in mainstream ticketing platforms (e.g., the category reviewed on the very G2/Capterra ecosystem this signal came from). The described pain likely reflects under-configured tooling, a low-tier plan, or a basic/shared-inbox setup rather than an unserved market gap. This is general market knowledge, not derived from the provided evidence.

The economic cost, if the 15-20 min/day figure is accurate, plausibly lands in the low tens of thousands of dollars per year for a mid-size team — meaningful but below the threshold that typically triggers a new software purchase on its own.
Because incumbents bundle routing into platforms teams already pay for, a standalone solution would face extreme competition and a near-zero switching rationale for most buyers.
assumptions: Assumes the team in SIG-0004 uses a ticketing system that lacks or has poorly configured routing — the evidence does not name the tool.
Assumes the '15-20 mins daily' figure is representative beyond one team — no corroboration exists.
Assumes the team lead's manual triage time is incremental cost rather than an accepted part of the role.
unknowns: Which ticketing tool(s) the affected teams use and whether routing features are available but unused.
Team size, ticket volume, and industry of the source — all of which drastically change pain severity.
Whether any buyer has paid, or attempted to pay, to solve this specific problem.
